title: oidc_relying_party plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `oidc_relying_party` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component OidcRelyingPartyConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

OidcRelyingPartyConfig.description: Plugin: oidc_relying_party — Browser OIDC relying party with authorization code + PKCE and encrypted sessions. ID token verification requires a JWT header kid that selects exactly one current trusted JWKS key; missing, empty, and unknown kid values are rejected with no all-keys fallback. Optional string fields accept null as "unset", matching constructor admission. Sessions too large for one browser cookie are split across bounded `<cookie_name>.N` chunk cookies.

issuer.description: Expected ID token issuer, compared as an exact case-sensitive string. Per RFC 7519 section 4.1.1 a present iss must be a single string; an array, object, number, boolean, or null iss is rejected. A discovery document is used only when its own `issuer` member is exactly this value (OpenID Connect Discovery section 4.3).

discovery_url.description: OIDC discovery URL. Mutually exclusive with authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and jwks_uri. The document must carry an `issuer` exactly equal to `issuer`. Its endpoints must use HTTPS and may live on other origins (Google and Microsoft Entra ID publish cross-origin endpoints); plain HTTP is accepted only for a loopback development discovery_url and only on its own origin. Every gateway-dialed URL (discovery_url, token_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint, jwks_uri, and discovered endpoints) admits plain HTTP only for a loopback IP-literal host (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1]), never for the name localhost, because DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects; configured browser-followed URLs (authorization_endpoint, end_session_endpoint, redirect_uri, post_logout_redirect_uri) and the issuer identifier keep the localhost development case, while a discovered plaintext endpoint must share the loopback IP-literal discovery origin. With client_auth.method none, a discovered token_endpoint must also be a loopback IP literal, and a discovered revocation_endpoint that is not one is ignored (logout skips revocation).

userinfo_endpoint.description: Optional UserInfo endpoint. When set alongside discovery_url, the explicit value overrides the UserInfo endpoint advertised by the discovery document, including one that omits it, and the discarded advertisement is not validated.

jwks_source.description: Admin-managed JWKS record used to verify ID tokens instead of fetching jwks_uri: `managed://jwks/<id>#jwks` (also accepted: `managed://jwks/<id>`, `managed://<id>#jwks`), stored through `/admin/tls/jwks`. Only with explicit authorization_endpoint and token_endpoint; mutually exclusive with jwks_uri and discovery_url. The fragment and collection must select JWKS material and `?` options are refused. The record is read from this node's managed TLS store (`FERRUM_TLS_MANAGED_STORE_PATH`): fresh while it is present, every key withdrawn (ID tokens refused) once it is deleted or holds no usable signing key, re-read every 900 seconds, on an unknown kid, and immediately after a local `/admin/tls/jwks` write. Admin writes refuse a reference to a record that does not exist; file mode refuses to start without it. Namespace-bounded operator tokens may not introduce one.

end_session_endpoint.description: Optional end-session endpoint used for RP-initiated logout. When set alongside discovery_url, the explicit value overrides the end-session endpoint advertised by the discovery document, including one that omits it, and the discarded advertisement is not validated.

post_logout_redirect_uri.description: Absolute HTTPS redirect URI sent to the provider after RP-initiated logout; HTTP is allowed only for localhost or literal loopback development endpoints.

method.description: Null or absent selects client_secret_basic. A non-string value is rejected. "none" is admitted only for a token endpoint whose host is a loopback IP literal (the name localhost does not qualify), including a token endpoint learned from discovery.

client_secret.description: Literal client secret. Plugin config is never environment-expanded; a value containing a `${NAME}` placeholder is refused at admission.

private_key_pem.description: Must support private_key_jwt_alg; admission signs a throwaway assertion, so a key on the wrong curve or of the wrong family is rejected at config load.

private_key_jwt_alg.description: Null or absent selects RS256. A non-string value is rejected for every method.

private_key_jwt_kid.description: Null or absent sends no kid header. A non-string value is rejected for every method.

redirect_uri.description: Absolute callback URI registered with the provider, with no fragment (RFC 6749 §3.1.2). Before issuing a browser challenge, Ferrum requires its host to match the validated request Host/:authority; DNS comparison is case-insensitive, IP literals compare by address, and ports are ignored. Trailing-dot DNS callback hosts and missing, malformed, or cross-host request authorities fail closed before state or cookies are issued.

callback_path.description: Callback path handled by Ferrum; must equal the path in redirect_uri. Also the correlation cookie's Path attribute, so it carries cookie-path syntax rules. Must already be a canonical request path (no percent-escapes, empty segments, dot segments, or backslashes), because it is compared with the frontend's canonical request path; dot segments are refused by the constructor.

logout_path.description: Must not resolve to the same path as callback_path; the callback branch is evaluated first. Must be a canonical request path, like callback_path. Logout is state-changing, so GET/HEAD requests must carry `Sec-Fetch-Site` same-origin or none, a POST is refused only when the browser reports cross-site or same-site, and other methods answer 405; a refused request clears nothing and contacts no provider.

claim_headers.description: Session claim path to upstream header mappings. Destination headers are gateway-owned and always sanitized: every configured destination is removed from the client request (case-insensitively) before verified claim values are installed, so an absent, null, empty, or wrong-type claim leaves the header absent instead of forwarding client-supplied input. Destinations in the gateway-owned `x-consumer-*` consumer assertion namespace and `x-authenticated-identity` are rejected at config load. At most 16 mappings; claim paths are at most 256 bytes with no whitespace or control characters, header names at most 128 bytes, and two mappings may not name the same header. Framing, provenance, credential-bearing and gateway-reserved destinations (including cookie, content-length, forwarded, via, x-real-ip, x-forwarded-* and x-ferrum-*) are rejected, as for output_claim_headers. In both forms reserved names and duplicates are matched case-insensitively with _ treated as - (X_Real_IP is reserved, X_Tenant_Id duplicates X-Tenant-Id, including across jwks_auth claim_headers and output_claim_headers). A claim value that is not a valid header value (for example one containing CR or LF) or that renders to more than 8192 bytes, including a joined array, leaves the destination absent.

id_token_clock_skew_secs.description: Leeway added to the ID token exp when deciding whether the session's claims are still live. The ID token exp is an RFC 7519 section 2 NumericDate (a JSON number that may carry a fractional part) and is the session's authoritative claim lifetime, truncated toward the past; it does not fall back to session.ttl_secs or the access-token lifetime. The session is still additionally capped by session.ttl_secs and session.idle_ttl_secs.

authorization_params.description: Static extra authorization-request parameters, such as `prompt`, `acr_values`, `login_hint`, or `ui_locales`, appended after the parameters the plugin owns. Names the plugin sets (response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, nonce, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, max_age, response_mode, request, request_uri) are rejected case-insensitively; values must not contain control characters.

max_age_secs.description: OpenID Connect `max_age`. When set it is sent on the authorization request, the callback requires an ID token `auth_time` no older than this (plus id_token_clock_skew_secs), and a session whose login is older re-challenges instead of refreshing.

forward_access_token.description: Relay the session's current (refreshed) access token to the backend as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. When enabled the backend Authorization header is gateway-owned on this route: every client-supplied copy is removed first, so a request whose accepted principal is not this session forwards none.

encryption_secret.description: AEAD key material for durable session cookies and sealed pending authorization-code correlation cookies; must be at least 32 bytes and must not be a known published or placeholder value (including the documented `${OIDC_SESSION_SECRET_32_BYTES_MIN}` placeholder, the key Ferrum Foundry's OIDC template published, Ferrum's own sequential example/test secrets, and obvious placeholders such as changeme, change-me, replace-me, placeholder, or your-secret). Screening covers both the supplied value and the effective key material (standard Base64 decoded only when it yields at least 32 bytes, otherwise raw bytes before HKDF), including Base64 spellings of denied values and unresolved `${...}` templates anywhere in either textual value. A rejected value returns 400 naming this field without revealing the secret.

encryption_secret_previous.description: Previous encryption secret accepted while rotating session and pending-flow cookies within the same versioned OIDC context; subject to the same raw and effective-key screening as encryption_secret, including Base64 spellings of denied values and unresolved `${...}` templates anywhere in either textual value. A rejected value returns 400 naming this field without revealing the secret.

cookie_name.description: Explicit cookie name opts out of automatic naming and must be an RFC 6265 cookie-name token. An explicit __Host- name additionally requires secure with no domain and a root path, and an explicit __Secure- name requires secure. When omitted, the context-derived name is prefixed __Host- when secure with no domain and a root path, __Secure- when secure otherwise, and left unprefixed when secure is false because browsers reject a prefixed cookie without Secure.

ttl_secs.description: Absolute session lifetime. Bounded so it can take part in Unix-timestamp arithmetic on every authenticated request.

max_cookie_bytes.description: Maximum encoded size of the sealed session value and of sealed pending-flow correlation cookies. The minimum is what a sealed pending authorization flow needs before any original-URL bytes. A session whose complete Set-Cookie line would exceed 4000 bytes is split across `<cookie_name>.0`…`<cookie_name>.N` chunk cookies (at most 9) that each fit a browser cookie; a session above this cap is refused at the callback with a named error instead of being emitted. Every session cookie carries Max-Age equal to the remaining absolute session lifetime. Not part of the session context, and it bounds only what is issued: existing sessions and in-flight logins up to the 8000-byte admission maximum stay readable after it is lowered.

secure.description: When false, generated session and correlation cookie names carry no __Host-/__Secure- prefix, because a prefixed cookie without Secure is rejected by browsers. Secure correlation cookies always use __Host- with Path=/ and no Domain.

same_site.description: Case-insensitive; normalized to lower case. "none" requires secure=true.

domain.description: Optional bare DNS Domain attribute (leading dot allowed) for the durable session cookie. The short-lived sealed pending-flow correlation cookie never inherits this value; secure correlation cookies use __Host- with Path=/, while insecure loopback-development cookies are scoped to callback_path.

hide_session_cookie.description: Remove this plugin's own session and pending-flow correlation cookies from the Cookie header forwarded to the selected backend, leaving unrelated application cookies intact. The sealed session cookie is a complete replayable gateway credential and the upstream already receives the verified identity and claim headers, so passthrough must be an explicit opt-in.

state_cache_max_entries.description: Per-instance size of the pending-login replay cache (DoS admission). When it is full, further logins are still started as sealed-only flows (no local replay entry), each charged to its source under state_cache_max_entries_per_source, up to one more state_cache_max_entries; beyond that new login starts answer 503. Cross-replica callbacks use the sealed correlation cookie and do not require a shared state cache.

state_cache_max_entries_per_source.description: Per-instance maximum pending browser authorization flows started per resolved client IP, enforced whether or not the replay cache is full; must not exceed state_cache_max_entries.

trusted_redirect_hosts.description: Origins a post-login redirect may target, as `host` (the redirect_uri scheme's default port only) or `host:port`; an explicit default port (`host:443` for https) names the same origin as `host`. Hosts compare case-insensitively; an entry that is not a bare authority (path, query, fragment, or userinfo) is rejected. A target must also use redirect_uri's scheme and carry no userinfo, and a target containing an ASCII control character or a backslash is refused. An accepted target is emitted in its normalized URL form (for example lowercased host, default port omitted). The redirect_uri's own origin is always trusted; anything else lands on post_login_default_path.

refresh_skew_secs.description: Refresh lead time before token expiry; must not exceed session.ttl_secs / 2, which the constructor enforces across the two objects.

rp_initiated_logout.description: With an authentic session cookie, send id_token_hint on provider logout and attempt discovered refresh-token revocation within five seconds. Cookie copies remain valid within session and claims lifetime limits. Without a valid cookie, return the local logout page.

post_login_default_path.description: Redirect target when no trusted original URL exists. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed and a whitespace-only value is rejected. Emitted verbatim as Location, so it must not contain ASCII control characters or a backslash.
